name: printf
description: Prints its arguments according to a FORMAT, like the C printf function. In the format, %s is replaced by text, %d by an integer, %f by a decimal number, and \n adds a newline (printf never adds one on its own). If there are more arguments than %, the format is reused. More predictable than echo in scripts.

options.description: (bash) Stores the result in a variable instead of printing it.

arguments.name: FORMAT
arguments.description: Template: %s (text), %d (integer), %.2f (decimal with 2 digits), %-10s (text left-aligned over 10 characters), \n, \t.

arguments.name: ARGUMENT
arguments.description: Values inserted into the format, in order.

examples.explanation: Inserts the user name into the message.
The format is reused for each argument: one fruit per line.
Left-aligns a name over 10 characters and right-aligns a number over 5.
